title: Regional runway velocity and latency fallbacks — Aug 2026
summary: Concise planning sheet that lays out three capacity scenarios (conservative / base / aggressive) across NA, EU, APAC for the next 9 months, maps expected utilization bands, and defines latency fallback rules and warm-pool sizing. Focus: align ramp windows with SLA-preserving fallbacks and burst capacity triggers.
body:
Context:
- Runway planning requested by product & SRE to ensure predictable latency under demand growth and cloud supply variability. This is a short-form planning sheet — not the full ops runbook.

Key assumptions (base case):
- Per-region traffic growth: NA +18% q/q, EU +14% q/q, APAC +22% q/q (driven by new enterprise pilots in APAC).
- Typical per-vGPU sustained throughput: 120k requests/day (mixed-latency workloads).
- Warm-pool target reduces cold-start tail by ~40ms on average.
- Fallback model (smaller quantized variant) increases latency by 8–25ms but preserves cost.

Projected capacity table (vGPU-equivalent units) — months: Sep26 / Dec26 / Mar27 / Jun27 (conservative | base | aggressive):
- NA: 120 | 160 | 220 | 300 (conservative)
- NA: 150 | 200 | 280 | 370 (base)
- NA: 180 | 240 | 340 | 460 (aggressive)

- EU: 80 | 100 | 130 | 170 (conservative)
- EU: 100 | 125 | 165 | 220 (base)
- EU: 120 | 150 | 200 | 270 (aggressive)

- APAC: 60 | 90 | 130 | 190 (conservative)
- APAC: 80 | 120 | 180 | 260 (base)
- APAC: 100 | 150 | 230 | 340 (aggressive)

Expected utilization bands (tokens/day demand vs capacity) — base case:
- Sep26: NA 65% | EU 58% | APAC 62%
- Dec26: NA 72% | EU 66% | APAC 75%
- Mar27: NA 78% | EU 72% | APAC 84%
- Jun27: NA 81% | EU 76% | APAC 88%

Latency SLO mappings and fallback policy (per-region):
- Primary SLO: p95 <= 180ms for interactive chat & completion endpoints.
- Soft degrade: when p95 > 180ms and < 260ms for >5m, switch 20% traffic to quantized fallback model (Q8/Q4 depending on model family).
- Hard degrade: when p95 > 260ms for >10m or token queuing exceeds 50k tokens, escalate to region-wide burst allocation and move up to 50% traffic to fallback.
- Fallback ordering: local quantized model -> cross-region spill (latency-aware) -> lower-cost shared warm-pool.

Warm-pool sizing guidelines (base case):
- NA: keep warm-pool equal to 12% of active capacity (rounded to nearest 8 vGPUs) — reduces tail by ~40ms and improves throughput for burst windows.
- EU: 10% warm-pool.
- APAC: 15% warm-pool (higher due to new pilot churn).

Burst reserve and procurement notes:
- We plan a small on-demand burst reserve (cloud credits + reserved spot mix) per region sized for 24–48h of peak growth beyond committed capacity.
- APAC: recommend earlier procurement of reserved instances in target cloud zone due to longer vendor lead times.

Operational run-windows and rollout cadence (base scenario):
- Sep 2026: soft ramp — +25 vGPU NA, +20 vGPU EU, +40 vGPU APAC (enable warm-pools, flighting).
- Nov 2026: mid ramp — +60 vGPU NA, +30 vGPU EU, +60 vGPU APAC (start reserved contracts).
- Feb 2027: scale phase — +80 vGPU NA, +35 vGPU EU, +100 vGPU APAC (dedicated pools ready).
- May 2027: review & rebaseline depending on observed utilization.

Risk scenarios & triggers (short list):
- Cloud region procurement delay (APAC): if >30 days delay, accelerate cross-region spill plan and add extra warm-pool in NA/EU for critical tenants.
- Demand overshoot (actual > +40% month-over-month): signal to paused non-critical evaluations and enable 50% fallback.
- Spot eviction spike (>20% of burst reserve lost over 4h): switch to on-demand fallback and notify finance for emergency top-up.

Open questions / decision points:
- Quantization targets per model family (ask applied-ml for Q4 fidelity tests).
- Cost cap for fallback usage (product to define acceptable per-customer latency vs cost tradeoff).
- Which enterprise customers require hard isolation from cross-region spill (list from sales).

Action items (owner):
- Aisha: finalize APAC reserved procurement path and PO schedule by 2026-08-24.
- Marco: run fidelity tests on fallback models and report throughput/latency delta by 2026-08-28.
- Emily: add region-specific warm-pool autoscaling policy to the allocator repo (PR target 2026-09-03).
- Noah: instrument a synthetic traffic job that simulates 3x daily burst to validate warm-pool sizing (target run 2026-08-31).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; the full ops runbook (war-room procedures, SLA playbooks, and procurement forms) will be linked after decisions on quantization and procurement.
- Please comment directly on the Confluence draft or drop a note in #infra-runway for rapid sync.
